rootCausesFound: objects were never missing from the render scene: scene.traverse found the group, 9 meshes, inFrustum true, chainVisible true, opaque material — the picture was the problem, not the pipeline
framePose fitted the bounding SPHERE against the narrow axis of a portrait phone, parking the camera 11.3 m from a 1.8 m chair (~100 px on screen)
camera.aspect was stale after the phone surface unmounted and remounted the world, so taps and project() disagreed with the drawn pixels
R3F's whole-scene event raycast let decorations 1.9-2.6 m from the camera take every pointerdown before a chair further away
the world canvas runs on demand and store mutations never invalidated it, so move/rotate/resize changed the transforms and not the frame
fixed: framePose fits the object's box axis by axis (width/tan(hFov/2), height/tan(vFov/2), + halfDepth) instead of the sphere
CosmosObjectsLayer keeps camera.aspect equal to canvas width/height
CosmosObjectsLayer raycasts only its own object groups for selection and drag; decorations can no longer eat a tap
CosmosObjectsLayer calls invalidate() on every store change
ringSlot default moved from z 4 to z 7.2, out of the core's room cluster
window.__cosmosObjectsProbe() now reports scene membership, world matrix, frustum, layers, render order, materials, canvas wiring and a hit test

builders.garmentClassification: pattern-based textile representation; NOT a graded manufacturing-ready pattern

blocker: the object meshes were not observed on screen; the render path has not been proven in the built app
limitations: one emulated 384x661 Chromium viewport; Chromium emulation is not hardware testing
objects persisted from older rings can still sit inside the core's room cluster, where the core's sphere may stand in front of them
the probe's projected screen coordinates can lag the drawn frame by one step
no 3D gizmos: manipulation is the contextual strip, drag and typed commands
